segments: From the Chronography of Bar Hebraeus: on the remnant of the Christians.
And on the morning of Wednesday, the tenth of Kanun the First of the year 1436
of the Greeks [1124/1125 AD], that accursed woman and her son departed,
and Amir Ghazi entered.
And when he saw those who had survived the famine,
looking as if they had come out of the graves,
he encouraged them.
And he gave wheat to the farmers to sow,
and brought herds of oxen and sheep,
and the city began to be rehabilitated.
And the blessed Mar Michael says in this year that al-Mustazhir the Caliph died,
and al-Mustarshid his son arose [in his place].
And perhaps through the discrepancy in the course of the lunar years of the Arabs and the solar ones of the Greeks he erred.
And in the year 1437
[of the Greeks, 1125/1126 AD], the lord of Hamah was killed by the Franks near Kafartab.
And the Franks took Jabala.
They pressed Tyre until {OCR?} the ships of the Venetians [and] Franks arrived,
and the king of Jerusalem also came to their aid,
and after fierce battles they took it.
And Malik 'Arab gathered an army,
and marched against his brother Mas'ud, Sultan of Iconium,
because he had made an agreement with the son of Danishmand.
Mas'ud, however, fled to Constantinople,
and was joyfully received by John, the king of the Greeks.
And he gave him an army and much gold,
and he set out and came to Ghazi.
And they both marched against Malik 'Arab,
and 'Arab fled to Thoros (Theodorus?), the Armenian ruler of Cilicia.
In this year, which is the year 520
of the Arabs [1126 AD],
ten Ismailis rushed upon Aq Sunqur Bursuqi, the amir of Mosul, in the great old mosque in Mosul,
and he killed three of them with his own hands,
and then he was killed.
And in his place his son 'Izz al-Din Mas'ud was established in power over Mosul, the Island of Qardu (Jazirat Ibn 'Umar), Mesopotamia, Aleppo, Hamah, and elsewhere.
And having lived for one year, he died.
And his younger brother succeeded him,
and Amir Jawali became his administrator,
who was a Turkish amir,
one of the slaves of his father al-Bursuqi.
And this Jawali sent the Qadi of Mosul,
namely Abu'l-Hasan 'Ali ibn Shahrazuri,
and Salah Yaghbisani as envoys to Baghdad to the Sultan,
to confirm the dominion for the young son of al-Bursuqi.
They, however, when they went, said to the Sultan:
"Mosul [depends] upon a man...
